rules.title: AI-ish vocabulary swapped for a plainer word
rules.description: Thirty words the upstream treats as AI register, each replaced by one of three plainer alternatives picked at random. Substitution, not deletion: the sentence survives, only the register changes.
rules.detection: Lexical. 30 literal watched word(s), matched case-insensitively via re.escape(word) with IGNORECASE, at most one replacement per word per pass (src/methodologies/postprocess.py:49-52).
rules.rewriteGuidance: Replace the word with a plainer one from its list. The upstream chooses at random among the alternatives; a caller should pick by context instead, because "utilize" is not always "use". Only the first occurrence of each word is replaced, so a repeated tell survives one pass.

watchPhrases.note: also | plus | on top of that
build | set up | put in place
use | take advantage of | tap into
never seen before | unheard of | groundbreaking

notes: Derived id vocab-replacement from the constant AI_VOCAB_REPLACEMENTS (src/methodologies/postprocess.py:6) and the method that applies it, _replace_ai_vocabulary (src/methodologies/postprocess.py:47).
30 entries extracted; the documentation claims "30+ English signal words" (docs/techniques.md:144), which matches the code.
Replacement lists are notes on the watched phrases, not detection data: the detector matches the source word, and the alternative is what the rewrite should produce.

0 key(s) are shorter than the 4-character floor the shared phrase classifier uses for Latin text (extract/phrase.ts:115), so those names are labelled literal here rather than reference, because a lexical detector must watch them, and with word boundaries they match safely: .
1 key(s) are hyphenated and need a word-boundary regex that treats "-" as a letter, not a terminator: cutting-edge.
The upstream does not strip punctuation before matching, so "utilize," is replaced and "utilization" is not; the substitution is a word, not a stem.

RECORDED TELL, NOT A RULE OF ITS OWN: the map itself is built with an em-dash join at src/methodologies/postprocess.py:67 (the merged sentence separator), and the em-dash is a catalogued tell. It belongs to rhythm-merge-short-sentences and is noted there; a separate rule would double-charge one piece of punctuation.

rules.title: Formal or academic vocabulary replaced with everyday words
rules.description: The same instruction as the vocabulary map, stated again as an LLM prompt: replace formal or academic vocabulary with everyday equivalents.
rules.detection: Model-judged. The upstream states the target register but never lists the words, so no watched phrase is derivable from this source and none is invented here.
rules.rewriteGuidance: Replace any formal or academic vocabulary with everyday equivalents, and add colloquial expressions where they fit. The wording is the upstream prompt, kept verbatim so a caller can reuse it; the model decides which words qualify.
rules.quote: replace any formal or academic vocabulary with everyday equivalents
notes: Derived id vocab-formal-to-everyday from the leading instruction of REWRITE_PROMPTS[1] (llm_rewriter.py:20).

Separate rule from vocab-replacement because it is a separate upstream artefact with a separate locator, but the same canonical signature, so cross-upstream dedupe still collapses the lineage to one problem.
Carries no watchPhrases: the upstream names a register, not words. The English word list lives in the other rule, which is why that one has 30 and this one has none.

rules.title: Consecutive short sentences merged into one
rules.description: Two consecutive sentences that are both shorter than 8 words are merged into one, with the separator replacing the full stop and the second sentence lowercased. The effect is fewer, longer sentences and a more even length profile.
rules.detection: Deterministic. Split on /(?<=[.!?])\s+/ and merge when both sentences are strictly under 8 words (config key postprocess.short_sentence_threshold, src/methodologies/postprocess.py:45). No-op below three sentences (src/methodologies/postprocess.py:57).
rules.rewriteGuidance: Merging two short sentences is only right when they belong together. The upstream does it positionally: any two consecutive sentences under 8 words get joined, regardless of whether they share a subject.
notes: Derived id rhythm-merge-short-sentences from the method name _disrupt_sentence_rhythm (src/methodologies/postprocess.py:55) plus the one thing the body does: merge two short sentences.
Threshold read from the default at src/methodologies/postprocess.py:45 (postprocess.short_sentence_threshold = 8); the upstream calls it a "short sentence" threshold in a config key, not a constant.

EM-DASH TELL (src/methodologies/postprocess.py:67): the merge inserts " — " as the separator, so the rule's own output uses a dash as the universal connector. That is itself an AI tell and the canonical vocabulary already has a signature for it (rhythm.dash_overuse). Recorded as a note and located precisely rather than extracted as a second rule, because the same line would otherwise deduct twice for one edit. The link is deliberately not asserted as `=> rhythm.dash_overuse` on the rule, so the extraction stays free of any relationship the type system does not model.

Off-by-one worth knowing: src/methodologies/postprocess.py:67 indexes sentences[i + 1][0] without a length check, so a second sentence that is pure whitespace-stripped to one character would produce an empty tail. Recorded as an upstream defect, not imported as behaviour.
The technique is rhythm.uniform_rhythm, not a punctuation rule: the tell being treated is uniform sentence length, and the dash is incidental to how this implementation attacks it.

The word count used is str.split() on whitespace, so a Chinese sentence counts as one "word" and the merge fires on almost any two Chinese sentences; see the src/methodologies/postprocess.py:56 segmentation note in the statistical port.

rules.title: Sentence lengths alternated by instruction
rules.description: The upstream asks a model to alternate between very short sentences of 3-8 words and long complex ones of 25-40 words, which is a direct instruction to raise burstiness.
rules.detection: Model-judged. The prompt states word-count bands but ships no checker, so nothing can be verified offline; the bands are recorded as the upstream states them.
rules.rewriteGuidance: Rewrite the text with dramatically varied sentence lengths, alternating between very short sentences (3-8 words) and longer complex ones (25-40 words); use natural, conversational vocabulary and preserve all factual content.
rules.quote: Rewrite the following text with dramatically varied sentence lengths.
notes: Derived id rhythm-alternate-lengths from the leading instruction of REWRITE_PROMPTS[0] (src/methodologies/llm_rewriter.py:16), "Rewrite the following text with dramatically varied sentence lengths".

REWRITE_PROMPTS[2] (src/methodologies/llm_rewriter.py:24) repeats the same correction as "ensure smooth transitions" and "no three consecutive sentences have similar length"; folded in here so one technique is one rule. That sentence is quoted in the documentation too (docs/techniques.md:149) as a post-processing rule, but the post-processor never checks length beyond the two-neighbour merge, so it exists only as prompt text.
Both this rule and rhythm-merge-short-sentences map to rhythm.uniform_rhythm on purpose: they are two implementations of one tell, and the dedupe key is the tell.
No word band is machine-checked anywhere in the repository, so the 3-8 and 25-40 bands are quoted from the prompt rather than encoded as detection.

disclosures: Documented but not implemented, so deliberately not a rule: 11+ Chinese boilerplate phrases with natural alternatives. No such list exists in the repository; `AI_VOCAB_REPLACEMENTS` at postprocess.py:7-36 holds English words only and the string "Chinese" appears in no Python source file. (docs/techniques.md:145)

Documented but not implemented, so deliberately not a rule: Detect and break 3+ sentence uniform-length patterns. `_disrupt_sentence_rhythm` only merges (postprocess.py:60-72): it never splits a sentence, and the only length test is `< short_threshold` on two neighbours. (docs/techniques.md:149)

Documented but not implemented, so deliberately not a rule: Insert transitional variety (short interjection, question, aside). Nothing in the post-processor inserts text other than the em-dash join; the adjacent prompt wording (llm_rewriter.py:21) delegates it to a model and cannot be checked. (docs/techniques.md:150)

Documented but not implemented, so deliberately not a rule: Segment selection by vocabulary diversity and by structural difference from the original. `_score_naturalness` (mixed_engine.py:28-35) scores a back-translation on unique-token ratio and word-length variance, both computed on the candidate alone, so the original is never consulted and no structural comparison exists. (docs/techniques.md:173-174)

Documented but not implemented, so deliberately not a rule: n-gram diversity as a statistical feature. `StatisticalDetector.score` (detectors/statistical.py:8-39) computes TTR, sentence-length CV and hapax ratio; there is no n-gram of any order in the file. (docs/techniques.md:138)

Documented but not implemented, so deliberately not a rule: Yule's K measure. The string 'yule' does not occur anywhere in the repository, and the detector returns a three-term mean, not four. (docs/techniques.md:139)

Documented but not implemented, so deliberately not a rule: DeepL as a mixed-engine member. `_get_translator` (mixed_engine.py:18-23) accepts only "google" and "mymemory" and raises ValueError otherwise. (docs/techniques.md:181)

Documented but not implemented, so deliberately not a rule: Apertium as a mixed-engine member. Same guard; the engine name appears in the repository only inside docs/techniques.md. (docs/techniques.md:182)

Methodology note, deliberately not a rule: the default execution path is a four-stage remote translation chain (src/standard/pipeline.py:5-8 and :82-98): LLM rewrite EN->ZH, LLM rewrite ZH->JA, Google Translate JA->FI, Niutrans FI->target. It needs an LLM key, a Niutrans key and an undocumented Google endpoint, so it is excluded from the extracted rules and must not become a default strategy. The offline statistical detector in statistical.ts is the only always-available asset.
